entities.name: Query NodQ protein
observations: 634 aa protein with strong homology to reviewed Rhizobium NodQ proteins; 60–64% identity over approximately 96–98% of the sequence.
Contains a GTP_EFTU domain at residues 25–210, a GTP-eEF1A_C region at 332–431, and an APS_kinase domain at 459–609.
The architecture supports a bifunctional sulfate-activation enzyme with an N-terminal GTPase-related module and a C-terminal APS kinase module.

entities.name: Bacterial NodQ
observations: Reviewed homologs are annotated as bifunctional enzymes involved in providing activated sulfate for Nod-factor modification or sulfate assimilation.
Curated homolog annotations include GTPase activity, ATP binding, sulfate adenylyltransferase activity, and adenylylsulfate kinase activity.
NodQ may associate physically with NodP sulfate-activating enzymes; the GTPase module is proposed to regulate ATP sulfurylase activity.

entities.name: Sulfate adenylyltransferase
observations: Chemical reaction: sulfate + ATP + H+ → adenosine 5'-phosphosulfate (APS) + diphosphate (PPi).
This is the ATP sulfurylase reaction and is mapped to Rhea RHEA:18133 in the retrieved homolog annotations.

entities.name: Adenylylsulfate kinase
observations: Chemical reaction: adenosine 5'-phosphosulfate (APS) + ATP → 3'-phosphoadenylyl sulfate (PAPS) + ADP + H+.
This is the APS kinase reaction and is mapped to Rhea RHEA:24152 in the retrieved homolog annotations.

entities.name: Sulfate assimilation
observations: The NodQ homologs are annotated in sulfate assimilation and activated-sulfate production pathways.
